hints: Start with the four symbols given for the wire: force $F$ with area $A$, and extension $x$ with original length $L$.
Recall that stress is $F/A$ and strain is $x/L$, and that Young modulus $E$ applies while Hooke's law is obeyed.
Form $E = stress/strain$ using those fractions and check which option has $F/A$ divided by strain.
walkthrough: Identify the definitions: tensile stress $= F/A$ and tensile strain $= x/L$ for the wire of length $L$ and area $A$.
State the governing rule: Young modulus $E = stress/strain$ for a material obeying Hooke's law.
Substitute the definitions: $E = (F/A)/(x/L)$, which can also be written as $FL/(Ax)$.
Compare with the options: only the form $F$ divided by $A \times strain$ equals $(F/A)/strain$.

options.A: Since strain is $x/L$, this is $stress \times strain$, not $stress/strain$.
options.B: Since stress is $F/A$, this is $stress/strain$, which is the definition of Young modulus $E$.
options.C: This is $(F/A) \times (x/L)$, which equals $stress \times strain$, not $stress/strain$.
options.D: Young modulus is $stress/strain$, so this fraction is inverted and equals $1/E$.
